connector: Today the book becomes a play. You pick a scene and read it out loud, with a voice for each character. Is the prince bossy or scared? Is Betsy calm or loud? Let the punctuation tell your voice what to do.

a.raw: does everyone hate me the prince asked
a.fixed: “Does everyone hate me?” the prince asked.
a.why: The prince asks a question, so a question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark. Does gets a capital D. The word the stays small, because the sentence keeps going. A period ends it.

b.raw: what about you the prince asked
b.why: The prince asks a question, so a question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark. What gets a capital W. The word the stays small. A period ends it.

mfill1.h1: Say con, then struct, then ion. Push them together.
mfill1.why: con + struct + ion = construction: the work of building.

mfill2.h1: Say in, then struct, then ion. Push them together.
mfill2.why: in + struct + ion = instruction: teaching, or steps that tell you how.

mfill3.h1: Say de, then struct, then ion. Push them together.
mfill3.why: de + struct + ion = destruction: tearing something down.

mfill4.h1: Say ob, then struct. Push them together.
mfill4.why: ob + struct = obstruct: to block the way.

vcloze1.h1: This one is about showing feelings with your voice and face.

vcloze2.h1: This one is the words the characters say to each other.
vcloze2.why: dialogue is the words characters say.

vcloze3.h1: This one is about reading smoothly, not choppy.
vcloze3.why: fluency means reading smoothly at the right speed.

vcloze4.h1: This one is the hardest word: rhythm, speed and stress.
vcloze4.why: prosody is the rhythm and stress of your voice.

gfill2.h1: Two people ran. Which bank word stands for both of them?

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Today the book turns into a play! You pick a scene and read it out loud, with a voice for each character. Is the prince bossy? Is Betsy loud? Let the marks on the page tell your voice what to do.
transcripts.guide1: Word work. You’ll build four new struct words, use pronouns so a name isn’t said twice, and join small words into compound words.
transcripts.guide2: No new chapters today. Pick the scene you would most like to read out loud. Think about how each character sounds.
transcripts.guide3: Today you check the pronouns in your comparison paragraph.

notes.wordParts: The root struct means build. construct = to build together. structure = something built. instruct = to build knowledge in someone.
notes.grammar: A pronoun takes the place of a noun. Doing the action: I, he, she, we, they. Getting the action: me, him, her, us, them. Showing whose: my, his, her, their.
notes.spelling: A compound word is two small words joined into one: rain + bow = rainbow. Read each part on its own, then blend them. A long word is not always a compound word.
notes.wgrd: Good readers hear each character’s voice. The marks on the page tell your voice when to rise, ask, or pause.
vocab: showing feelings with your voice, face, or body
reading smoothly at the right speed
the rhythm and stress of your voice

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Every character in this book sounds different. The prince sounds bossy, Betsy sounds bold, and Jemmy talks like the streets. Today you read a scene out loud, so listen for each voice. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you look back. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one is from Chapter 17. Steady on your legs? Jemmy asked. It's a question, so the question mark goes inside the quotation marks. And asked starts with a small letter, because the sentence keeps going. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Say the parts out loud. Type the whole word in each box. Tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Look what one little ending can do. Act, plus i o n. Action! The ending i o n turns a doing word into a thing. Today you'll stick it on struct words, and you'll add some front parts too. Say the parts out loud, push them together, and type the whole word. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Here's a reading-aloud word that's not in your bank. Pause. When you pause, you stop for just a moment, like at a comma. Reader's Theater is full of pauses! Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Read the Remember box. Type a pronoun from the word bank in each blank.
mods.script: Listen to this. Betsy fed Betsy's bear, and Betsy's bear licked Betsy. Clunky! Let's fix it. Betsy fed her bear, and the bear licked her. Much better. Read the Remember box. Then type a pronoun from the word bank in each blank, so no name is said twice.

mods.todo: Tap each card to join the two small words. Then answer the question in the box.
mods.script: Oops. I wrote foot, then a space, then ball. But a football is one thing, so it's one word. Foot and ball join right up, with no space. Tap each card to join the two small words. Say the new word out loud. Then answer the question in the box.
Try reading this out loud. Which way is south? Straight on! You certain? Certain I'm certain. Jemmy sounds lost. Betsy sounds sure of herself. Can you hear the difference in your own voice?

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then look back through the whole book.
mods.script: There are no new chapters today. Read the two Pause and Think questions first. Then flip through the book and find the scene you'd most like to read out loud. Read it in your head first. How should each character sound? Then do the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now answer in full sentences. One, which scene did you pick, and which chapter is it in? Two, read it out loud two times, and tell how your reading changed. Three, how should each character sound? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Find one pronoun in your comparison paragraph. Check it, and write the sentence the right way.
mods.script: Today you check your pronouns. Clara found this: Both him and Jemmy changed. Cover Jemmy. Him changed? No. He changed. So she fixed it. Find one pronoun in your comparison paragraph. Check it the same way, and write the sentence the right way.

items.t: In Chapter 18, Smudge holds out his hand. The prince shakes it, even though no one is allowed to shake a prince’s hand.
items.why: He tries something new and treats Smudge like a friend.

items.t: In Chapter 2, the prince tells the tutor, “I can always get someone to write my name for me.”
items.why: He won’t try something hard. He wants someone else to do it.

items.t: In Chapter 17, Betsy runs up to the two outlaws and shouts, “Stop it!”
items.why: She stands up to two bullies to help a boy she doesn’t even know.
